messages:
maria: Quick note — ran a focused nsys pass to investigate weird tail latency when KV evictions and small batches co-occurred. Sharing the flags and a small playbook we used so others don't repeat the same mistakes.

akshay: nice, pls drop the exact command and any env tweaks. also what was the workload (seq len / batch / kv size)?

maria: Command we used (trimmed):

maria: ```
nsys profile \
  --output=nv-3745-playbook.qdrep \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --duration=45 \
  --capture-range=osrt:1:bracketed \
  --capture-range-frames=3-8 \
  --capture-memory-io=true \
  --sample-frequency=1000 \
  --force-overwrite \
  --wait \
  -- python -u run_infer.py --model=model-v1 --batch=8 --seq=1024 --kv-max-entries=256
```

maria: Notes on those flags:
- --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt: need all three. cuda gives kernel timeline, nvtx maps our spans (batch start/finish), osrt provides user-space sampler events that correlate with kernel scheduling.
- --sample=cpu + --sample-frequency=1000: cheap way to get lightweight sampling without blowing up file size. we increased sample-frequency to catch short-lived scheduling stalls.
- --duration=45: bracket captures < 10s often miss the rare KV-evict spike; 30–60s windows work well.
- --capture-range=osrt:bracketed + --capture-range-frames: use nvtx/osrt markers to bracket warmup then the steady-state window.

jordan: workload: 8-way batch, seq=1024, kv entries ~200 on average, synthetic replay to keep traffic steady. we added a 2-iteration warmup outside the capture window to populate kv-cache.

akshay: any envs? kernel prefetch / affinity?

maria: yes:
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinned to single GPU for the run.
- export TF_ENABLE_CUBLAS_TENSOR_OP_MATH=1 (our runtime toggles tensor ops per model).
- for reproducible sampling: disable background service jobs on the node and set scheduler affinity for worker threads: taskset -c 2-11 python ...

maria: Observations from the trace:
- kernel timeline showed repeated short spikes of a kernel named kv_cache_evict (~80–120us) that coincided with a blocking kernel gemm_fp16 (~200–300us) right after.
- the evict kernels appear in bursts correlated to when batch sizes briefly dropped to 1–2 due to an upstream queue hiccup.
- osrt sampler traces showed concurrent host-side GC-like pauses from the batcher thread (we had a lock contention).

jordan: root cause hypothesis: batching heuristic lets a lonely request bypass batch-aggregation if queue wait > X ms; when that happens we trigger a different code path that does an eager KV eviction (to reduce memory footprint), which runs on the GPU and contends with gemm kernels.

akshay: solution ideas?

maria: short-term: increase the batching wait threshold so tiny straggler batches get held for a beat and coalesced. also make evict async where possible (schedule on a separate stream and use stream priorities).

maria: capture tips we learned (so you don't lose the signal):
- avoid very short total capture windows (<10s) unless you can reproduce the spike reliably.
- bracketed captures with osrt/nvtx markers: emit NVTX push/pop at (warmup end) and (warmup end + window) so you only record the steady-state frames.
- use --sample-frequency higher than default when kernels are <200us, otherwise sampling will miss them.
- if file size grows too big, drop cuda-memory or reduce duration, but keep nvtx/osrt.

akshay: how did you validate the async-evict idea?

maria: prototyped: two changes — batch wait + evict on low-priority stream. re-ran same nsys flags and saw:
- kv_cache_evict kernels still present but shifted to lower priority stream and no longer overlapping gemm_fp16 on the high-priority compute stream.
- tail p99 latency dropped ~18% across runs.

jordan: command to extract hot kernels we used: 

jordan: ```
nsys stats nv-3745-playbook.qdrep --report=trace --report-output=nv-3745-trace.csv
# then quick awk to aggregate by kernel name
cat nv-3745-trace.csv | awk -F, '{print $6}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
```

maria: a couple more heuristics for future captures:
- when debugging kernel selection, also capture small synthetic runs where seq-length distribution is skewed to short/long to force kernel switch. kernels chosen by our runtime change for seq<128 vs seq>512 and those transitions are often where we mis-pick kernels.
- tag NVTX with metadata like batch_size, seq_len, kv_entries so the timeline shows context.

ci-bot: pinned: /eng-runtime perf-playbook. (automated note)

akshay: awesome, can you drop this into the perf runbook (short checklist) and add the sample-frequency rationale?

maria: will do. I'll also attach the qdrep and a small timeline screenshot to the runbook entry. :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks — saved me a huge investigation time. if anyone else runs similar traces, ping me so I can help correlate kernel names to runtime ops.

maria: thanks all.
